note: Nominal literature values for isotropic thermal conductivity and density at approximately room temperature. None of these values is qualified: no source is cited per value, no temperature dependence is modeled, and no specific alloy, grade, or supplier is named. They are round, commonly cited textbook/datasheet figures suitable for a screening-level design search, not a materials-certification record.

graphite.note: Real graphite is strongly anisotropic: pyrolytic sheet can exceed 1000 W/m-K in-plane and run under 10 W/m-K through-plane, depending on grade and processing. This model treats every material as isotropic (materials.json states one conductivity, and the finite-element solver applies it in every direction), so 150 W/m-K is a single nominal value for bulk isostatic/isotropic graphite, not a claim about any anisotropic sheet product.
